runtime.execution: Bun/Effect process with instance-scoped session runners, AI SDK or feature-gated native provider streams, child shell/MCP processes and background session jobs.
runtime.service_boundary: Owns local sessions, tool settlement, runners and launched stdio children; consumes model providers and MCP/service APIs. Local child disposal is distinct from governing independent shared services.

summary: A session-oriented coding agent with a durable normalized conversation/tool record, per-step model/tool resolution, JS/TS tool and plugin hooks, managed summaries and optionally concurrent child sessions.

inspection.scope: Read entry/loop/provider dispatch, tool settlement, shell execution, child resumption/background delivery, cancellation, compaction selection and pruning, message retrieval, plugin/config lifecycle, native schemas and relevant test excerpts. Source inspection only.
inspection.limits: Inspected excerpts rather than every file/branch. Default AI SDK transport internals, complete native-provider/GitLab workflow implementation and every optional tool dispatch were not traced. Experimental flags materially gate child background work and richer event emission. No reference code or tests executed.

actions.name: SessionPrompt.prompt / loop
actions.input: sessionID plus user parts, model/agent and optional noReply/tools overrides
actions.output: persisted user message and final assistant result
actions.lifecycle: persists then continues provider/tool steps; instance runner owns cancellation
actions.authority: server/program caller; tool rules merge agent and session policy

actions.name: shell
actions.input: command; optional timeout in ms, workdir; description
actions.output: bounded streamed preview, final text, exit code and full-output file path when truncated
actions.lifecycle: awaited spawn races exit/timeout/abort; abort/timeout request termination; no public reusable shell process handle established
actions.authority: model under shell/external-directory rules and environment hook

actions.name: read
actions.input: filePath; optional one-based offset and limit
actions.output: numbered text/directory entries or image/PDF attachment
actions.lifecycle: single read; media/binary and clipping rules apply
actions.authority: model with path permission checks; full read wrapper not fully inspected

actions.name: write
actions.output: write result, diff and diagnostics metadata
actions.lifecycle: permission then write, formatting and events
actions.authority: model; edit permission may ask operator

actions.name: glob / grep
actions.output: bounded file list or file/line/text search results
actions.lifecycle: awaited search-service query with cancellation signal

actions.name: apply_patch
actions.output: patch result; full mutation/result path not traced
actions.lifecycle: registered native tool parses hunks; schema/source boundary disclosed
actions.authority: model through common tool permission context

actions.name: task
actions.input: description, prompt, subagent_type; optional task_id, command, background
actions.output: child task_id and terminal text, or running background status
actions.lifecycle: new/resumed child session; feature-gated background start/extend; terminal parent notification; cancellation propagates
actions.authority: model with task permission and child-agent restrictions

actions.name: todowrite
actions.input: todos with content, status and priority

actions.name: question
actions.output: operator answers associated with the originating call
actions.authority: model can request operator input when this client/agent exposes the tool

actions.name: skill
actions.output: instruction text and sampled resource paths
actions.lifecycle: lookup/read; no standalone workflow execution inferred

actions.name: webfetch / websearch
actions.output: fetch/search output; complete transport/error semantics not inspected

actions.name: lsp / plan_exit
actions.output: language-service result or operator plan-transition question; complete latter dispatch not traced
actions.lifecycle: conditional registration; optional behavior is not unconditional baseline
actions.authority: model under LSP policy; operator answers planning transition

actions.name: custom JS/TS and plugin tools; named hooks
actions.input: tool schemas/execute implementations; named hook input and mutable output
actions.output: custom tool outputs with clipping; altered request/context/tool output
actions.lifecycle: instance-cached imports; named hooks awaited; event callbacks fire asynchronously; dispose callbacks on teardown
actions.authority: operator-authored extensions; model can edit files when filesystem policy permits, but automatic live reload not established

actions.name: MCP tools
actions.input: discovered server JSON schemas and named arguments
actions.output: MCP content converted into tool outputs/attachments
actions.lifecycle: request timeout; local stdio child lifetime tied to instance; remote servers consumed
actions.authority: model under merged tool permissions; server configured by operator/program

actions.name: messages / message / config.update
actions.input: session/message ID and optional limit/before; configuration patch
actions.lifecycle: retrieval does not restore context by itself; config update marks instance for disposal
actions.authority: operator/program API; not a dedicated model audit/repair tool

filesystem.detail: Read, write, edit, glob and grep are registered model operations with path checks, bounded output and edit policy.

processes.detail: shell spawns and streams an OS command, records exit/overflow metadata and races exit, timeout and abort. Reusable process/PTY handles were not established.

code_actions.detail: Model-written shell programs and custom JS/TS tool implementations can compose computation; the default provider interface still dispatches named JSON-schema tools rather than a persistent code-action interpreter.

persistent_kernel.detail: No model-addressable persistent interpreter was established in the inspected shell, tool registry and session loop. Instance/server memory and fresh shell spawns do not establish such a kernel.

standing_database.detail: Internal session storage and todo updates are visible, but no model-queryable standing structured database contract was established in this loop/tool/MCP study. External MCP composition remains possible, not traced.

workflow_programming.detail: Custom JS/TS tools, before/after execution hooks and message/compaction transformations provide executable composition. A replaceable first-class workflow scheduler was not established.

multi_model.detail: The loop resolves the selected model each provider step; child agents may override the parent's model. This does not itself create live collaboration.

live_collaboration.detail: Experimental background tasks accept updates addressed by task_id while busy and later inject terminal notifications into the parent. Inspected wiring is parent-child session/task routing, not a general peer-room or arbitrary bidirectional live bus.

concurrent_work.detail: Feature-gated background child jobs expose task/session identity, extension and completion; independent job work can overlap the parent. Their lifetime is still linked to cancellation/instance scope.

steering_interrupt.detail: New user turns become reminders on later loop steps; cancellation propagates through session descendants, provider AbortController and shell race/termination. Remote providers acknowledging cancellation was not validated.

turn_redefinition.detail: Message transformations, compaction prompt hooks, tool replacement and per-step model/tool resolution can alter a continuation's inputs. The main while-loop's scheduling program is not shown as a hot-replaced turn definition.

compaction.detail: Overflow/pending compaction yields a persisted tool-free summary and retained tail boundary. Pruning marks prior outputs; active-message filtering uses summaries/tail_start_id. Hook-supplied prompts/context are supported.

context_repair.detail: Original stored messages remain retrievable through server message APIs after active-context filtering; output-file paths support further inspection. No dedicated model repair/lineage operation is established, and clipped-output originals have an expiry.

original_audit.detail: Durable normalized message/tool settlement is useful, but complete original provider/program/transformation capture is not established. Raw chunks are selectively enabled, richer events are gated and separate full-output files expire after seven days.

audit_query.detail: Program callers can retrieve all/paged session messages or a message by ID; models can read/search known overflow files. This queries the retained conversation/output scope, not a demonstrated complete audit corpus.

hot_change.detail: Tools/plugins are instance-cached and config.update marks the instance for disposal. Inspected code does not enforce Arconaut's default activation after affected turns/workflows conclude; disposal finalizers cancel owned work.

rebuild_continuity.detail: Stored sessions support conversation retrieval, while instance teardown cancels runners and closes/kills owned MCP children. No executable rebuild/outpost handoff retaining unresolved owned work was established.

remote_services.detail: MCP tool calls consume service schemas/results; local stdio servers are explicitly launched and disposed by the instance. Remote transport reconnect/session-continuity details were outside inspected excerpts.

self_improvement.detail: Normal file/shell access and custom plugins provide editing capability. The inspected loop, extension lifecycle and tests do not establish a dedicated model-governed candidate/evaluate/promote harness-improvement program.

complaints.detail: The native registry, question/todo and session APIs inspected do not establish a model-invokable complaint operation capturing agent state and follow-up. This is not a claim about all uninspected plugins.

authority.detail: Standing permission rules merge agent/session policy. Defaults allow most actions but ask on selected sensitive scopes; build and plan agents have different edit policies. Models act through these rules and can request operator answers.

evaluation.detail: Inspected tests directly assert busy-child update identity/completion ordering and compaction tail boundary. Mocked provider/prompt streams make these local orchestration oracles, not provider integration or semantic summary-fidelity validation.

time_order.detail: Message/call IDs and stored wall timestamps support turn/tool ordering; Effect durations enforce shell/request deadlines. A specified monotonic, restart or paused-time contract was not established.

evidence.claim: prompt persists a user message, updates session permission overrides and starts the loop unless noReply.
The continuing loop filters compacted messages, handles pending tasks/compaction, resolves current model/agent/tools and transforms messages before processor.process.
Processor results drive stop or compaction; interruption finalizes the assistant message and the session runner owns the loop.
Default streamText gets prepared tools/messages, provider middleware and scoped AbortController; raw chunks are enabled specifically for Copilot.
Call IDs identify running tool parts; successful and failed results settle durable parts, completion Deferreds and timestamps.
Registry tools and MCP tools receive context, merged permission asks and before/after plugin hooks; tools are invoked through execute.
Instance-cached custom JS/TS and plugin tool discovery is composed with built-ins; LSP, questions and plan tools have gates.
shell accepts command, optional positive timeout, workdir and description.
Spawned shell output streams through bounded tails and overflow files; exit, abort and timeout race, with termination and exit metadata.
task accepts prompt, description, subagent_type, task_id, command and background; permission checks and child-session/model selection precede execution.

Child prompt execution returns its last text; busy background task extension, completion notifications, same task_id resumption and cancellation are wired but background requires an experimental flag.
Instance-scoped runners are canceled at disposal; explicit cancellation traverses descendant background jobs and startShell rejects a busy runner.
Pruning marks old completed tool outputs with compacted timestamps rather than deleting their stored output in this path.
Compaction plugins can alter prompt/context; selected history becomes a tool-free summarizing request and tail_start_id is persisted.
Completed summaries and retained tail boundaries control the filtered active message sequence.
Large outputs have separately written originals, with a seven-day cleanup policy and line/byte clipping defaults.
Configuration hooks run during instance initialization; event hooks and awaited named mutable-output hooks are available, with disposal callbacks.
Config API updates project configuration then marks the instance for disposal.
Session messages can be retrieved in full, paginated or by message ID through the server API.
Default permissions allow most actions but ask for doom loops, external directories and environment files; primary/plan agents merge distinct restrictions.
MCP schemas become tools and client.callTool sends named arguments with a request timeout.
Local MCP creates a stdio child using command, arguments, cwd and environment.
Clients are initialized concurrently and instance disposal terminates stdio descendants and closes connected clients.
Read returns directories, typed image/PDF attachments or numbered text with offset/limit and binary/truncation checks.
write accepts content and filePath, asks edit permission with a diff, writes/format-checks and publishes changes.
edit accepts oldString/newString/replaceAll, serializes file access and asks permission before writing.
grep validates roots/permissions and asks the search service for file/line/text results with abort.
glob checks root permissions and returns bounded matching files with a truncation indication.
question awaits operator answers associated with session and tool IDs.
todowrite updates session todos after permission checking and returns structured JSON.
skill resolves named instruction material, asks permission and returns text plus sampled resource paths.
Gated lsp defines location/query operations and performs external-directory and lsp permission checks; dispatch beyond this excerpt was not traced.
webfetch declares URL, format and timeout and asks webfetch permission; the complete fetch/error path was not traced.
websearch selects a configured search provider and dispatches query/search settings; remote transport behavior was not traced.
apply_patch takes nonempty patchText and begins parsing patch hunks; full mutation behavior was not traced.
plan_exit has an empty argument schema and asks the operator about moving from planning to building.
Background subagents, LSP, plan mode and event-system features have experimental gates; native LLM has its own flag.
Mocked prompt responses and Deferreds test that a running child update keeps its task identity and completion/notification waits for the updated run.
A seeded three-turn test asserts persisted tail_start_id points at the second user turn under a two-turn retention configuration.

tests.focus: Busy child task update and completion notification ordering.
tests.oracle: Deferred mocked prompts prove task_id stability and that completion/notification uses the updated result; no live provider, room delivery or OS process cancellation is tested by this case.

tests.focus: Retained recent-turn boundary and overflow arithmetic.
tests.oracle: Seeded history asserts tail_start_id for the second of three turns; canned LLM streams isolate orchestration and do not establish summary semantic fidelity.

strengths: Durable tool-call identity and explicit success/error settlement decouple tool execution from display.
Per-step model/tool resolution plus named extension hooks provide several concrete intervention boundaries.
Retained-tail summaries and logical output pruning preserve a recoverable stored conversation scope.
Busy-child update handling has a concrete identity/order oracle rather than only a background-task claim.
limits: Useful experimental child/event behavior is gated and should not be assigned to every default deployment.
Normalized conversation storage and expiring overflow files do not satisfy full original audit requirements.
Instance disposal cancels owned work; config invalidation is not a quiescent executable refit.
Some optional native tools were inspected at schema/registration boundary only; complete dispatch semantics remain outside this row.
arconaut_questions: Which changes should resolve per provider step, and which must wait for the affected turn/workflow boundary?
How should busy addressed participants receive steering without reducing live collaboration to parent-child terminal notifications?
How can compaction lineage and every original provider/program output remain queryable independently of active context or output retention cleanup?
Which local children belong to harness quiescence, and which independent services must survive refit without being governed by Arconaut?
